new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, pool at tick -50 with active liquidity L1 from [-100, 100). An attacker adds a position over [-20, 100) with liquidity L2 larger than L1, which does not change active liquidity at -50. A trader makes the first taxed zero-for-one swap of a block and the tick stays at -50. initDown(-50, -50) leaves currentTick at 0, so CompensationPriceFinder.getZeroForOne visits ticks 0 and -20, and liquidity.sub(L2) reverts the swap. With a smaller L2 the swap goes through with wrong liquidity, and if the first pass returns early, the second pass after reset continues from the stale position and adds reward growth to ticks that were never crossed. The posthoc test in forge_P8_posthoc.json, a taxed swap that keeps a negative tick, passes against this repair.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep04.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 before the search, which includes the start tick in every non-empty range. But it also moved the currentTick assignment below the empty-range return, so when start equals end the iterator keeps a stale currentTick and can return ticks.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep05.summary: When the start tick is aligned and initialized, the patch skips the advance only if the start sits at bit 0 or no lower initialized tick is in the same bitmap word. Otherwise it still calls _advanceToNextDown, which skips the start tick.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep06.summary: Calls _advanceToNextDown only when the start tick is not a multiple of the tick spacing or its bitmap bit is clear. An aligned, initialized start tick stays as currentTick and is returned first.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep07.summary: Replaces the call to _advanceToNextDown with a loop that searches the start word from the start tick's own bit, then moves down one word at a time until it finds an initialized tick or the word's lowest tick is at or below the end tick. The start tick is returned whenever it is initialized, and the loop is bounded by the end tick.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep08.summary: The repair returns the start tick first when it equals normalizeUnchecked(startTick), which means it is a multiple of the spacing, and its bitmap bit is set. Otherwise it advances strictly below the start as before. The rule covers unaligned, negative and word-edge starts.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep09.summary: The repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing, the end tick is not, and the start tick's net liquidity is negative. In every other case an initialized start tick is still skipped, which is why attack P5 still works.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep10.summary: When the start tick is aligned and initialized, the patch keeps it only if it sits at bit 0 or no lower initialized tick is in the same bitmap word. Otherwise it still calls _advanceToNextDown, which skips the start tick.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep11.summary: After the empty-range return, the repair increments currentTick to startTick + 1, so the search covers ticks at or below the start in the word that reset loads. This is the same rule as the reference repair. The unchecked increment cannot overflow for a real pool tick.

codex_openai/P-E2/rep12.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 just before _advanceToNextDown, so the first search includes the start tick.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep01.summary: Clears the word for an empty range and loads the bitmap word of the tick just below the start instead of the start's own word. The current tick is still the start tick, so _advanceToNextDown still searches strictly below it and the walk is unchanged.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep02.summary: Only moves the empty-range return below the bitmap load. The search still starts strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep03.summary: The repair loads the bitmap word of compress(startTick - 1) instead of compress(startTick). _advanceToNextDown uses or reloads that same word anyway, so the walk is unchanged and still skips an initialized start tick.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep04.summary: Only moves the empty-range return below the bitmap load. The search still starts strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep05.summary: Moves the bitmap word load above the empty-range check and changes nothing else. The current tick is still the start tick when _advanceToNextDown runs, so an initialized start tick is skipped as before.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep06.summary: The repair loads the bitmap word of compress(startTick - 1) instead of compress(startTick), and also loads a word in the empty-range case. _advanceToNextDown would use or reload that same word anyway, so the walk is unchanged and still skips an initialized start tick.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep07.summary: Loads the bitmap word of startTick - 1 instead of startTick and clears currentWord on an empty range. The search still begins strictly below the start tick, so the walk is unchanged and an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep08.summary: Moves the bitmap load above the empty-range return and adds a branch for a start of type(int24).min, which can never run because the start then equals the end. The search still starts strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep09.summary: Adds a revert when either tick is outside MIN_TICK to MAX_TICK and loads the bitmap word before the empty-range return. The search still starts strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep10.summary: The repair only moves the empty-range return below the bitmap load. The walk still searches strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped and all five attacks still work.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep11.summary: The repair moves the empty-range return below the bitmap load and sets currentTick to type(int24).min in that case. The walk for a non-empty range is unchanged and still skips an initialized start tick, so all five attacks still work.

openhands_openai/L-E2/rep12.summary: Only moves the empty-range return below the bitmap load. The search still starts strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep01.summary: Returns the start tick first only when it is a multiple of the tick spacing and its net liquidity, read from the pool manager, is not zero. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep02.summary: Reads the start tick's net liquidity from the pool manager and, when it is not zero, sets the current tick to the start plus one so the search includes the start. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep03.summary: When the start tick is a multiple of the tick spacing, sets the current tick to the start plus one so the search in _advanceToNextDown includes it; unaligned starts keep the audited path, which already includes the rounded-down tick. It also loads the start word before the empty-range check.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep04.summary: Returns early when the start tick is a multiple of the tick spacing and its bitmap bit is set, so getNext yields it first. Otherwise it calls _advanceToNextDown as before.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep05.summary: After loading the start word, returns early with the current tick at the start when the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and its bit is set, so getNext yields it first. All other starts keep the audited path, which is already correct for them.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep06.summary: Sets currentTick to the aligned tick one step above the start's compressed position, using bit 0 of the next word when the start sits at bit 255, then calls _advanceToNextDown. The existing search therefore begins at the start tick's own bit.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep07.summary: The repair returns early with currentTick on the start tick when the start is a multiple of the spacing and its bitmap bit is set. Otherwise it advances strictly below the start as before. The rule covers unaligned, negative and word-edge starts.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep08.summary: Keeps the empty-range return with currentTick at the start, then sets currentTick to startTick + 1 so the existing search begins at the start tick's own bit. This matches the reference repair.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep09.summary: Replaces the call to _advanceToNextDown in reset with its own word-by-word search that starts at the start tick's own bit and stops once the current tick is at or below the end tick. It returns an initialized start tick and handles unaligned, negative and word-boundary starts.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep10.summary: The repair sets currentTick to the start tick rounded down to a multiple of the spacing. If that tick's bit is set it is returned first, otherwise the walk advances strictly below it. This includes an initialized start tick and handles unaligned, negative and word-edge starts. For an empty range currentTick is at or below the end tick, so hasNext is false.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep11.summary: After the empty-range return and the bitmap load, the repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1, so the search covers ticks at or below the start. This is the same rule as the reference repair.

openhands_openai/P-E0/rep12.summary: If the start tick equals the tick of its own bitmap position, which means it is aligned, and that bit is set, reset returns with currentTick at the start tick so getNext returns it first. Otherwise it calls _advanceToNextDown as before.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep01.summary: Sets the current tick to the start tick plus one after the empty-range check, so the search in _advanceToNextDown begins at the start tick itself. This is the same rule as the reference repair.

new_flaw.description: The repair drops a tick that the audited code returned. When the start tick has negative net liquidity, the first initialized tick below it is also skipped if its net liquidity is positive. The hook then never updates that tick's reward growth and carries the wrong liquidity below it. This adds to the original bug rather than replacing it.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, positions [0, 100) with L and [50, 300) with L2, where L is much larger than L2. A taxed zero-for-one swap moves the tick from 100 to 20. The walk returns no ticks (the audited code at least returned tick 50), so the hook spreads the whole tax over L2. The real liquidity at tick 20 is L. The [0, 100) position is credited about L/L2 times the tax, paid out of other LPs' rewards.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep02.summary: The repair still searches strictly below the start tick, so an initialized start tick is never returned. When the start tick's net liquidity is negative, it also skips the next initialized tick if that tick's net liquidity is positive. This avoids the liquidity underflow revert (attacks P1, P2, P4 and P5 no longer revert) but leaves the start tick skipped (P3 still steals 48.9 ETH). The hiding is done inside reset itself, not in another function.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep03.summary: For an aligned start tick, reads the tick's liquidityNet from the pool and keeps the start tick only when liquidityNet is not zero. An initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep04.summary: Returns early when the start tick is a multiple of the tick spacing and its bitmap bit is set, so getNext yields it first. Otherwise it calls _advanceToNextDown as before.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep05.summary: After loading the start word, reset finds the highest set bit at or below the start's bit and returns early if that bit is the start tick itself, so getNext yields it first. In every other case it calls _advanceToNextDown as before.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep06.summary: After the empty-range return, sets currentTick to startTick + 1 so that _advanceToNextDown searches at or below the start tick.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep07.summary: Sets currentTick to the start tick rounded down to a multiple of the tick spacing and calls _advanceToNextDown only when that tick is above endTick and its bitmap bit is clear. If the rounded tick is initialized and above endTick, it is returned first.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep08.summary: The repair returns early, leaving currentTick on startTick, whenever the bitmap bit of compress(startTick) is set. This returns an initialized aligned start tick, but for an unaligned start whose rounded-down tick is initialized it returns the unaligned start tick itself. The extra tick has zero net liquidity and the hook only writes reward growth to an unaligned tick that no position can use, so I found no new High or Medium flaw.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep09.summary: Rewrites reset with its own loop that searches from the start tick's own bit and stops at the bitmap word that holds the end tick. It returns an initialized start tick, and when nothing initialized lies above the end tick it sets the current tick to the end tick so hasNext is false.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep10.summary: The repair returns the start tick first when the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and its bitmap bit is set. Otherwise it advances strictly below the start as before. Signed modulo gives 0 only for aligned ticks, so the rule covers unaligned and negative starts, and the word cache stays valid at bit 0 and bit 255.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep11.summary: Loads the start word before the empty-range return, then sets currentTick to startTick + 1 so that _advanceToNextDown searches at or below the start tick.

openhands_openai/P-E1/rep12.summary: After loading the start word, sets the current tick to the start tick plus one inside an unchecked block, so the search in _advanceToNextDown begins at the start tick itself. This is the same rule as the reference repair.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep01.summary: Sets the current tick to the start tick plus one after loading the start word, so the search in _advanceToNextDown begins at the start tick itself. This is the same rule as the reference repair.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep02.summary: Keeps the start tick only when its bitmap bit is set, it is not bit 0, and no lower bit in the same word is set. Otherwise the initialized start tick is still skipped, and an unaligned start that passes the check is itself returned although it is not initialized.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep03.summary: Keeps the start tick when its net liquidity is not zero and otherwise calls _advanceToNextDown. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep04.summary: Keeps the start tick when its liquidityGross is not zero and otherwise calls _advanceToNextDown. In Uniswap v4 a tick's bitmap bit is set exactly when its liquidityGross is not zero, and unaligned ticks store no liquidity, so this matches the bitmap.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep05.summary: Returns the start tick first only when the start is a multiple of the tick spacing, the end tick is not, and the start's net liquidity is not zero. With an aligned end tick, or a start tick whose net liquidity is zero, the start tick is still skipped, which is why attack P5 still works.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep06.summary: Keeps an aligned, initialized start tick only when it is bit 0 of its word or no lower bit in the same word is set. When another initialized tick sits below it in the same word, the start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep07.summary: When the start tick is aligned and initialized, the patch keeps it only if it sits at bit 0 or no lower initialized tick is in the same bitmap word. Otherwise it still calls _advanceToNextDown, which skips the start tick.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep08.summary: Runs a copy of the downward search first and keeps the start tick only when the end tick is not aligned, another initialized tick lies between start and end, and the start tick's net liquidity is not zero. In all other cases the initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep09.summary: Keeps the start tick only when its net liquidity is not zero and the end tick is not a multiple of the tick spacing. When the end tick is aligned or the net liquidity is zero, the initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep10.summary: The repair keeps currentTick at the start tick only when that tick has non-zero gross and net liquidity and the next initialized tick below it in the same bitmap word is not the end tick. Start ticks whose next lower tick is the end tick, or whose net liquidity is zero, are still skipped.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep11.summary: When the start tick is a multiple of the tick spacing and its bitmap bit is set, reset keeps it as the first tick, but only if its net liquidity is not zero. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

new_flaw.description: The search loop that the repair adds to reset does not stop at the end tick. It keeps loading lower bitmap words until it finds any initialized tick, and stops only at word type(int16).min. Gas therefore grows with the distance to the next initialized tick below the start, not with the swap range.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, only position [100, 200), pool tick 50 with no active liquidity. A taxed zero-for-one swap moves the tick from 50 to 40. Each of the two reset calls loads every word from 0 down to -32768, about 32,800 external reads or roughly 90 million gas, so the swap runs out of gas. With tick spacing 1 and only a full-range position, a one-tick swap near tick 0 makes each reset load about 3,500 words, where the audited code loads one or two.

openhands_openai/P-E2/rep12.summary: The repair decides whether to include the start tick from outside state: always when the iterator is being reused, and for a fresh iterator only when the pool has zero active liquidity and its tick is the start or end tick. It also replaces the call to _advanceToNextDown with its own search loop that does not stop at the end tick.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep01.summary: When the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and its net liquidity, read from the pool manager, is not zero, sets the current tick to the start plus one inside an unchecked block so the search includes it. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep02.summary: After the bitmap load, the repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1, so _advanceToNextDown searches compress(startTick) inclusive in the word that was just loaded. This is the same rule as the reference repair. The guard for type(int24).max can never trigger for a real pool tick.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep03.summary: After the empty-range return, sets currentTick to startTick + 1 inside an unchecked block so the existing search begins at the start tick's own bit. This matches the reference repair; the unchecked add can only wrap for a start of type(int24).max, which is not a valid tick.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep04.summary: The repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and its net liquidity is non-zero. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped; every other case is handled correctly.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep05.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is aligned, the end tick is not aligned, and the start tick's liquidityNet is not zero. With an aligned end tick, or an initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero, the start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep06.summary: For an aligned start tick whose liquidityNet is not zero, sets currentTick to startTick + 1 so the search includes it. An initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep07.summary: The repair loads the word of compress(startTick) and sets currentTick to the aligned tick one compressed step above it, so _advanceToNextDown searches from compress(startTick) inclusive. At bit 255 that search reloads the same word. This includes the start tick and handles unaligned, negative and word-edge starts.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep08.summary: When the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and its net liquidity, read from the pool manager, is not zero, sets the current tick to the start plus one so the search includes it. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep09.summary: The repair loads the start word, keeps the empty-range return, and then sets currentTick to startTick + 1 before calling _advanceToNextDown, so the search covers ticks at or below the start. This is the same rule as the reference repair.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep10.summary: Starts the search at startTick + 1 only when the start tick is aligned and the end tick is not. When the end tick is a multiple of the tick spacing, the initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep11.summary: Sets the current tick to the start plus one only when the start is a multiple of the tick spacing and the iterator already held a non-zero tick or word before reset. The first walk after initDown still skips the start tick, so the price finder and the reward walk see different ticks, and attacks P2, P4 and P5 still work.

openhands_openai/R-E2/rep12.summary: After the empty-range return, which still leaves currentTick at the start, the patch sets currentTick to startTick + 1 so the existing search begins at the start tick's own bit. This matches the reference repair.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep01.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and the end tick is not. When the end tick is also a multiple of the spacing, an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep02.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is aligned, the end tick is not aligned, and the start tick's liquidityNet is not zero. With an aligned end tick, or an initialized start tick whose liquidityNet is zero, the start tick is still skipped.

new_flaw.description: The patch moved the line that sets the current tick below the empty-range return. When start equals end, the current tick keeps its old value: 0 for a fresh iterator from initDown, or wherever the last walk stopped. At a negative tick this makes hasNext true, so the walk yields tick 0 and the initialized ticks between 0 and the current tick, none of which the swap crossed. Example: tick spacing 60, pool at tick -300 with active liquidity L1, and a position [0, 600) with liquidity L2 larger than L1. A taxed zero-for-one swap that stays inside tick -300 gets tick 0 from the walk, the hook subtracts its net liquidity L2 from L1, and afterSwap reverts with ArithmeticOverflowUnderflow. Anyone can add such a position to block these swaps.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep03.summary: Sets the current tick to the start plus one only when the start is a multiple of the tick spacing, the end tick is not, the start is below type(int24).max, and the start's net liquidity is not zero. It also no longer sets the current tick for an empty range, so hasNext can be true when start equals end.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep04.summary: The repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and the end tick is not. When both are aligned, an initialized start tick is still skipped, which is why attack P5 still works.

new_flaw.description: For an empty range the walk returns startTick + 1, a tick above the start that the price never crossed. In the hook both walks then process that tick: they subtract its net liquidity from the active liquidity and add reward growth to rewardGrowthOutsideX128 for it.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 1, pool tick 100. An attacker adds an out-of-range position [101, 102). Each small zero-for-one swap that is the first taxed swap in a block and leaves the tick at 100 makes the hook credit reward growth to tick 101, so the attacker's position earns part of the tax without being in range. The rest of the tax is divided by the active liquidity minus the attacker's liquidity, so in-range positions are paid more than the tax collected. If the attacker's liquidity is larger than the active liquidity, the subtraction underflows and the swap reverts.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep05.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 at the top of reset, so the first search includes the start tick. Because this happens before the empty-range return, an empty range now has hasNext true and yields startTick + 1.

new_flaw.description: The search loop that replaces _advanceToNextDown in reset does not stop at the end tick. It keeps loading lower bitmap words until it finds any initialized tick, and stops only at word type(int16).min. Gas therefore grows with the distance to the next initialized tick below the start, not with the swap range.
new_flaw.scenario: Tick spacing 10, only position [100, 200), pool tick 50 with no active liquidity. A taxed zero-for-one swap moves the tick from 50 to 40. Each of the two reset calls loads every word from 0 down to -32768, about 32,800 external reads, so the swap runs out of gas. The post-hoc gas check in this folder (forge_P7_posthoc.json) used about 150 million gas for such a swap. With tick spacing 1 and only a full-range position, a one-tick swap near tick 0 makes each reset load about 3,500 words.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep06.summary: The repair replaces the call to _advanceToNextDown with its own loop that finds the highest initialized tick at or below compress(startTick). If that tick is above the end tick it becomes currentTick, otherwise hasNext is false. The ticks returned are correct in every case, but the loop does not stop at the end tick.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep07.summary: Keeps the start tick only when it is aligned, the end tick is not aligned, and the start tick's net liquidity is not zero. When the end tick is a multiple of the tick spacing, the initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep08.summary: The repair skips the call to _advanceToNextDown whenever the bitmap bit of compress(startTick) is set. This returns an initialized aligned start tick, but for an unaligned start whose rounded-down tick is initialized it returns the unaligned start tick itself. The extra tick has zero net liquidity and the hook only writes reward growth to an unaligned tick that no position can use, so I found no new High or Medium flaw.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep09.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 and calls _advanceToNextDown, so the first search includes the start tick. It keeps a separate alignment and bitmap check for startTick equal to type(int24).max, which is not a valid Uniswap tick.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep10.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 before the search, but only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and the end tick is not. When both are multiples of the spacing, an initialized start tick is still skipped.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep11.summary: Loads the start word before the empty-range return and replaces the first _advanceToNextDown call with a loop that searches from the start tick's own bit, one word at a time, until it finds a set bit above endTick or reaches endTick.

openhands_openai/RP-E2/rep12.summary: Sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and the end tick is not. When the end tick is also a multiple of the spacing, an initialized start tick is still skipped.
